message.content:
The earliest references to Jesus Christ in non‑biblical historical sources come from two Roman writers who lived within a few decades of his death:

| Source | Author | Date of Writing | Passage | What it says |
|--------|--------|-----------------|---------|--------------|
| **Antiquities of the Jews** | Flavius Josephus (Jewish historian) | c. 93–94 CE (Book 18, Chapter 3, Section 3) | “...the wise man Jesus, who was called the Christ, ... crucified by Pontius Pilate” | Mentions Jesus as a real person, a teacher, and notes his execution under Pilate. |
| **Annals** | Tacitus (Roman senator & historian) | c. 116 CE (Book 15, Chapter 44) | “Christus, the founder of the name, was executed by Pontius Pilate during the reign of Tiberius” | Confirms Jesus’ execution and the existence of a movement called Christianity. |

These are the earliest surviving references that scholars generally accept as independent attestations of Jesus’ historicity. Other early mentions (e.g., Pliny the Younger’s letter to Emperor Trajan, c. 112 CE) refer to Christians but do not mention Jesus by name.
message.reasoning: User asks: "What is the earliest reference of Jesus Christ in history from historical record?" They want earliest reference from historical record. We need to provide answer. According to scholarly consensus, earliest references are from Josephus (Antiquities 18.3.3) and Tacitus (Annals 15.44). Also maybe Pliny the Younger (letters). But earliest is Josephus. So answer: Josephus wrote about Jesus in Antiquities of the Jews, Book 18, Chapter 3, Section 3, around AD 93-94. Also Tacitus wrote about Christ in Annals 15.44 around AD 116. Provide details.
